first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both deteriorating, making simplification the most directly responsive option and potentially improving sustainable revenue through faster time-to-value without immediately sacrificing price realization. I would verify the archived onboarding result and the competing promotional-pricing evidence because both are consequential: onboarding may improve activity without qualified revenue, while discounts may recover SMB demand but erode revenue quality or retention. Run a guarded test measuring qualified pipeline, conversion, retention proxies, and revenue—not completion alone.

final.rationale: Run a standard simplification experiment because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and the verified result shows shortened onboarding improved completion, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. Do not use promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue 18% initially, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive renewal, conflicting with the sustainable-revenue objective. Measure qualified revenue, activation, time-to-value, and renewal/retention—not onboarding completion alone.
